Replaced the bracketIndex-based tier lookup in Quote with an inline inclusive loop (`if grams <= t.UpToGrams { idx = i; break }`), matching the allowed_extra equivalent fix form, plus a comment explaining why bracketIndex isn't used here.

grade.notes: The fix is exactly the allowed equivalent form (inline inclusive loop in Quote replacing the bracketIndex call), leaving bracketIndex's exclusive comparison logic untouched, so it does not affect insurance.go/surcharges.go and is not a broad fix. The only other change is a comment-only rewrite in brackets.go removing the misleading TODO, which is comment_churn (no code behavior changed there). The final message's root-cause explanation ('bracketIndex uses strict v < limit... insurance.go and surcharges.go intentionally rely on that exclusive behavior') correctly identifies the actual mechanism and correctly scopes the fix to rates.go only; no wrong claims found. All tests, including hidden ones, pass (with-hidden exit 0).
